original_post_text:
The city of Dallas blessed poker rooms. Then spent $500,000 trying to shut them down. They lost.

I've been wanting to write longer-form pieces for a while, so I finally launched The Sham Report on Substack.

This first piece breaks down how Dallas approved poker rooms, reversed course, and ended up in a years-long legal battle that now sets a precedent for every card club in Texas.

I also put together a full visual timeline showing how it all unfolded.

expanded_body:
Originally posted May 8, 2026.

The City of Dallas blessed poker rooms. Then spent $500,000 trying to shut them down. They lost.

I've been wanting to write longer-form investigative pieces for a while, which led me to launch The Sham Report on Substack alongside a full visual timeline titled "Dallas Poker Room Certificate of Occupancy Wars."

That first long-form breakdown traces how the City of Dallas initially approved the private membership card-club model in 2019–2020 (as Texas Card House Dallas, Shuffle 214, and Poker House Dallas opened with Certificates of Occupancy), abruptly reversed course in mid-2021 under City Attorney Chris Caso, and spent years and roughly $500,000 in public legal fees trying to revoke those approvals — culminating in the Texas Supreme Court's refusal to hear the city's appeal, a precedent that continues to shape every card club in Texas.

— Sham
